chunks: Your Lord has neither left you, nor despises you.

key_terms.قَلَىٰ: despised you / turned away with displeasure
key_terms.وَدَّعَكَ: left you / bid farewell to you

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God did not leave or despise the Prophet?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a reassurance of divine proximity (qurb) to the Prophet, emphasizing that God's love for him remains constant despite periods of silence in revelation. It underscores the concept of continuous divine grace (fadl) and serves as a source of comfort for the faithful during times of spiritual trial or perceived distance from the Divine.
